subject.title: [Feature]: Harden Control UI Lit lifecycle boundaries

question: Should the Control UI Lit lifecycle hardening land as one broad modernization slice or be split by lifecycle seam before implementation?
rationale: The source evidence supports the work, but the protected label and multi-surface refactor require maintainer intent on scope, sequencing, and proof before automation should act.

options.title: Split by lifecycle seam
options.body: Create separate PRs for shared host/i18n, external-source subscriptions, router pending/not-found state, and chat post-render/persistence teardown.

options.title: Land one coordinated refactor
options.body: Allow one larger modernization PR if the owner wants a single pass and it includes broad Control UI regression coverage plus browser proof.

options.title: Narrow to proven bugs
options.body: Defer shared abstractions and only fix individual source-proven lifecycle races as live or test reproductions are established.

recommendation.title: Split by lifecycle seam
recommendation.body: Create separate PRs for shared host/i18n, external-source subscriptions, router pending/not-found state, and chat post-render/persistence teardown.

likelyOwner.reason: shakkernerd has the strongest recent path-history signal across the Control UI architecture, app-host, sidebar, router, and chat-state files implicated here.
